findings.location: rows[1].pricing, chooseSection.body, alternatives[0].body, alternatives[6].body, faqs[0].answer, faqs[1].answer — e.g. "Zelle charges $0 to send or receive; a first-quarter 2026 survey found $0 send, receive and request fees at 99.40% of linked consumer accounts. Each participating bank sets its own sending limits" and "Zelle has no 1.75% instant cash-out fee; it also cannot fund a payment with a credit card or send money internationally. Individual banks set per-transaction and daily sending limits, so Zelle's consumer fee page gives no single network-wide dollar limit."
findings.issue: Neither zelle_home.txt nor zelle_fees.txt mentions sending limits, per-transaction or daily limits, or credit cards (0 hits for 'limit', 'daily', and 'card'). Those sources also state 'Typically, there are no fees for consumers to send or receive money with Zelle®. We recommend confirming with your bank or credit union that they do not charge fees for Zelle® transactions' alongside the Q1 2026 survey showing $0 fees at 99.40% of linked consumer accounts, rather than an unconditional 'Zelle charges $0'. In addition, alternatives[0].body paragraph 1 contains a 34-word sentence and paragraph 2 joins two independent clauses with a semicolon ('Zelle has no 1.75% instant cash-out fee; it also cannot...'), violating _content-standard.md PREFLIGHT and _anti-ai-language.md.
findings.fix: Ground all Zelle claims strictly in zelle_home.txt and zelle_fees.txt: (1) In rows[1].pricing write: "Typically $0 consumer fees to send or receive. A first-quarter 2026 survey found $0 send, receive and request fees at 99.40% of linked consumer checking and savings accounts. No dollar sending limits published on Zelle's homepage or consumer fee FAQ". (2) In chooseSection.body final sentence write: "Zelle's homepage and consumer fee page publish no dollar sending limits and advise checking with your financial institution." (3) In alternatives[0].body split the 34-word sentence into two sentences under 25 words, replace the semicolon with a period, replace the unsupported credit-card and daily/per-transaction limit claims with the documented facts that both parties must hold eligible US checking or savings accounts (no international sends) and that Zelle's checked pages list no dollar sending limits. (4) Update alternatives[6].body bullet 3 and faqs[0]/faqs[1] to match.

findings.location: rows[6].pricing, alternatives[5].body, alternatives[6].body, alternatives[7].body — e.g. "Fee shown in transfer quote; no fixed public fee table or transfer limits on the checked homepage. Fees vary by destination, delivery feature and funding method; currency conversion also contributes to Xoom's revenue" and "Fees vary by destination country, selected delivery feature and funding method."
findings.issue: xoom_root.txt line 85 states 'Service availability and fees vary by country, features selected and other factors. Individual and aggregate transaction limits may also apply. In addition to transaction fees, Xoom makes money when it changes your send currency into a different currency.' Nowhere in xoom_root.txt does Xoom mention 'funding method'. In addition, alternatives-daily-auto.md Page Rule 4 specifies starting cells for vendors without a published price table with 'Quote-based; no public price'.
findings.fix: Replace 'funding method' across rows[6].pricing, alternatives[5].body, alternatives[6].body bullet 4, and alternatives[7].body bullet 5 with Xoom's actual disclosure ('country, selected features and other factors'). Start rows[6].pricing with: "Quote-based; no public price on Xoom's homepage. Exact fee and recipient amount shown before sending. Fees vary by country, selected features and other factors, and currency conversion also generates revenue for Xoom".

findings.location: rows[4].pricing and alternatives[3].body — "Wise offers free local account details for receiving in 22 currencies." and "physical card $9" / "A Wise physical card costs $9 once, with no monthly subscription."
findings.issue: wise_pricing.txt line 113 states 'Getting account details to receive in 22 currencies: Free', while free non-wire domestic receipt applies in 9 currencies and SWIFT receipt applies in USD, GBP, EUR plus 'an additional 19 currencies' (22 total). Calling all 22 'local account details' misstates the source. Also, wise_pricing.txt lines 100-102 list 'Getting the Wise Multi-Currency Card / No subscription fees / 9 USD' without stating 'physical'.
findings.fix: In alternatives[3].body paragraph 2 change "free local account details for receiving in 22 currencies" to "free account details for receiving in 22 currencies". In rows[4].pricing change "physical card $9" to "Wise Multi-Currency Card $9", and in alternatives[3].body paragraph 3 change "A Wise physical card costs $9 once, with no monthly subscription." to "Getting a Wise Multi-Currency Card costs $9, with no subscription fees."

findings.location: alternatives[4].body paragraphs 2-3 — "Invoice payments by ACH cost 1%, with a $1 minimum. That fee has no cap on Free, a $10 cap on Plus and Premium, and a $5 cap through Square's application programming interface." and "Square Checking gives instant access to sales through a business debit card with $0 monthly fees. Square Savings lists a 1.00% annual percentage yield (APY) and no fees or minimums."
findings.issue: (1) In square_pricing.txt lines 1214-1227, 'ACH bank transfer (via API)' ('Applies to ACH transfers through the Web Payments SDK and Payments API: 1%, $1 min, $5 fee cap' across all three plans) is a separate transaction type from 'ACH bank transfer (via invoice)', not a cap on invoice ACH payments; starting with 'That fee' conflates the two rows and triggers backward-pronoun in _anti-ai-language.md. (2) In square_pricing.txt line 1377 (footnote 3), Square Savings accrues 1.00% APY 'per folder on folder balances over $10. APY is subject to change, and current as of Jan 23, 2026', and the ModernWallet site adapter (alternatives-daily-auto.md line 210) requires variable APYs to carry their published date ('APY as published on <date>'). Also, square_pricing.txt line 1159 calls Square Checking 'a free checking account' while '$0 monthly fees' is stated in footnote 3 for Square Savings.
findings.fix: In alternatives[4].body paragraph 2 write: "Invoice payments by ACH cost 1% with a $1 minimum, uncapped on Free and capped at $10 on Plus and Premium. ACH transfers through Square's web and payments application programming interfaces cost 1% with a $1 minimum and a $5 cap across all tiers." In paragraph 3 write: "Square Checking is a free business checking account that gives instant debit-card access to Square sales. Square Savings lists a 1.00% annual percentage yield (APY) on folder balances over $10 (APY as published on January 23, 2026), with $0 monthly fees and no minimum deposit to open."

findings.location: alternatives[2].body final sentence into alternatives[3].body paragraph 1 — "It also lacks the Venmo Business Profile and Tap to Pay merchant profile described here." (15 words) followed by four consecutive Wise sentences of 16, 16, 18, and 17 words
findings.issue: Fails GATE — Sentence rhythm in _content-standard.md ('5 or more consecutive sentences fall within 3 words of each other': lengths [15, 16, 16, 18, 17], spread = 3). In addition, 'described here' violates _content-standard.md PREFLIGHT ('When you mention the page itself: Do not.') and _anti-ai-language.md page self-reference, while apple_cash_terms.txt line 131 directly states 'You may not use the Services for business or commercial purposes.'
findings.fix: Replace the final sentence of alternatives[2].body with "Apple Cash terms also prohibit business or commercial use." (9 words), and shorten sentence 4 of alternatives[3].body to "Wise charges no monthly subscription fee." (6 words), changing the sequence to [9, 16, 16, 18, 6] and removing the page self-reference.

findings.location: intro paragraph 1 sentence 1 and faqs[0].answer sentence 1 — "Use Zelle for direct domestic bank transfers, PayPal or Apple Cash for wallet payments, Wise or Xoom for international transfers, and Square for business card payments instead of Venmo." and "Use Zelle for eligible US bank-to-bank payments, Apple Cash for payments between compatible Apple devices, or PayPal for wallet-based personal sends."
findings.issue: (1) Missing primary keyword 'Venmo alternatives' in the first paragraph of intro, failing alternatives-daily-auto.md Page Rule 5 (line 56) and _content-standard.md ## SEO (line 196: 'Use the primary keyword in the SEO title, H1, first paragraph, the closing next-action sentence, and 2-3 H2/H3 headings'). findings.fix: Rewrite intro sentence 1 as: "Zelle, PayPal, Apple Cash, Wise, Square and Xoom are six Venmo alternatives covering domestic bank transfers, personal wallets, international sends and business card payments." Rewrite faqs[0].answer sentence 1 as: "Zelle fits eligible US bank-to-bank payments, Apple Cash fits payments between compatible Apple devices, and PayPal fits wallet-based personal sends."

findings.location: alternatives[1].body paragraph 2 and alternatives[2].body paragraph 3 — "Currency conversion adds a 4.00% spread when the recipient receives another currency, or 3.00% on other conversions." and "At larger amounts, each schedule reaches its $25 fee cap: the percentage calculation reaches that level above $1,470.59 for Apple Cash and above $1,428.58 for Venmo."
findings.issue: (1) In paypal_fees.txt lines 415-420, PayPal's 4.00% spread (or other disclosed amount) also applies when paying for goods or services in another currency and on PayPal Payouts in another currency, with 3.00% (or other disclosed amount) on 'All other transactions'. (2) Unrounded 1.7% and 1.75% already exceed $25.00 at (not strictly above) $1,470.59 ($25.00003) and $1,428.58 ($25.00015), i.e. above $1,470.58 and $1,428.57, and because apple_cash_terms.txt line 64 rounds the 1.7% fee to the nearest cent, Apple Cash rounds to $25.00 starting at $1,470.30 ($24.9951).
findings.fix: In alternatives[1].body write: "Currency conversion adds a 4.00% spread when a personal or Payouts recipient gets another currency or on foreign-currency purchases, and 3.00% on other conversions (unless another rate is disclosed)." In alternatives[2].body write: "At larger amounts, each schedule hits its $25 fee cap: with nearest-cent rounding, Apple Cash reaches $25 at $1,470.30 ($1,470.59 unrounded), while Venmo's 1.75% reaches $25 at $1,428.58 unrounded."
